name: BQ7695201PFBR
title: BQ76952 family: 16-cell (3S to 16S) battery pack monitor and protector, Li-ion, Li-polymer, LiFePO4
summary: A monitor and protector for packs of 3 to 16 series cells, up to an 80 V stack with 85 V tolerance on the cell and high-voltage pins. Two ADCs measure every cell voltage and the pack current at the same time; a comparator-based protection set plus firmware checks can switch high-side NFETs driven from an internal charge pump, blow a chemical fuse, and balance cells, either on their own or under a host. It has two programmable LDOs for outside use, up to nine thermistor inputs, OTP for production settings, and I2C, SPI or HDQ. BQ7695201PFBR is the version that starts in SPI with CRC and REG1 off, in a 48-pin TQFP.

circuits.title: 16-series monitor (example board)
circuits.description: The monitor half of the 16-cell example board. Each of the 17 cell taps from J1-J3 reaches its VC pin through 20 Ω, with 220 nF across each adjacent pair of filtered taps; cell 1 instead has 220 nF from VC1 and from VC0 to VSS. BAT is fed from the top of the stack through a 100 V Schottky diode and 100 Ω and held up by 1 µF and 100 pF, so the chip rides through a pack short. CP1 has 0.47 µF to BAT. An FCX495TA driven from BREG makes REGIN from the CD node (between the charge and discharge FETs) through a 100 V Schottky diode and 300 Ω; REG1 feeds the 10 kΩ I2C pullups. Current is sensed in a 1 mΩ low-side resistor with 100 Ω into SRP and SRN and 0.1 µF plus 100 pF across them. Two thermistors sit on TS1 and TS3; TS2 has a jumper to ground through 10 kΩ for wake. RST_SHUT, ALERT and HDQ are pulled down through 1.0 kΩ, and CFETOFF and DFETOFF are tied to VSS. BAT- and VSS meet at a net tie.

Each has 10 MΩ gate to source and a 16 V zener clamp. CHG reaches Q2's gate through 5.1 kΩ. DSG reaches Q3's gate node through 10.2 kΩ (two 5.1 kΩ), in parallel with 7.50 kΩ in series with a 100 V Schottky diode (anode toward the gate), and 0 Ω runs from that node into the gate. Q4 (source at PACK+, drain at Q3's gate node) has 10 MΩ and a 16 V zener from gate to PACK+, and its gate meets PGND through 10 kΩ and a 100 V diode (anode at PGND). PACK and LD each sense PACK+ through 10.2 kΩ. Two 0.1 µF capacitors in series bridge PACK+ to PGND, two more bridge the stack top to PACK+, and a spark gap guards the output. operation.text: Five versions share one die and differ only in factory defaults: BQ76952 (I2C, no CRC, REG1 off), BQ7695201 (SPI with CRC, REG1 off), BQ7695202 (I2C with CRC, REG1 on at 3.3 V), BQ7695203 (SPI with CRC, REG1 on at 5 V) and BQ7695204 (SPI with CRC, REG1 on at 3.3 V).

Settings live in RAM registers that load from one-time-programmable memory at power-up. They can be written into OTP on the production line (with BAT at 10 V to 12 V and the die between -40°C and 45°C), or set by the host after every power cycle. Registers survive NORMAL, SLEEP and DEEPSLEEP; SHUTDOWN clears them. Full reconfiguration needs CONFIG_UPDATE mode, which halts measurement and protection until it is left.

SEALED, UNSEALED and FULLACCESS levels gate what can be read and written; each step needs its own key sent by subcommand. Only FULLACCESS can write OTP or enter CONFIG_UPDATE. Subcommands return signatures of instruction ROM, data ROM and the static configuration so corruption can be caught. A 32-byte scratchpad, writable to OTP in FULLACCESS, holds serial numbers or dates.

One multiplexed ADC reads all 16 differential cell voltages each loop, plus one of VC16/PACK/LD, one of internal temperature/reference/VSS, and up to three thermistor or ADCIN slots, so a loop has 18 to 21 slots of 3 ms (1.5 ms in fast mode); a full set takes three loops. Cell results are trimmed, calibrated and given in 1 mV units, with raw 24-bit counts also readable. Slower loop settings add idle slots and lower NORMAL-mode current.

With fewer than 16 cells, a spare VC pin can tap the far side of a long inter-cell link so its I·R drop is left out of both neighbouring cell readings, and the link resistance can be computed from the reported link voltage and synchronized current. Such taps keep the series R and filter C of a cell input. A spare input not used this way is shorted to the adjacent VC pin. A register marks which inputs are real cells so cell protections ignore the rest. No differential input may go below -0.3 V; -0.2 V is the recommended floor.

Rarely, a Cell 1 Voltage() reading taken in SLEEP is wrong. Read cell 1 at intervals longer than Power:Sleep:Voltage Time so three readings are distinct, and discard one that differs strongly from those before and after. A bad reading can set an SUV PF alert but not an SUV fault if the SUV delay is 1 s or more, and cannot trip CUV, which runs on a comparator; a reading below the CUV threshold with no CUV alert marks it as invalid.

TS1-TS3, CFETOFF, DFETOFF, HDQ, DCHG, DDSG and ALERT can serve as general ADC inputs referenced to the bandgap, limited to the REG18 voltage, with a digital full scale of about 2.02 V. Raw counts from TS1 are reported for factory calibration.

A low-side sense resistor feeds SRP and SRN through an RC filter, wired so charge current makes SRP positive. The coulomb counter ADC covers ±200 mV. CC1 gives a 16-bit value every 250 ms in NORMAL for charge integration; CC2 gives 24-bit current every 3 ms (1.5 ms in fast mode, lower resolution); CC3 averages up to 255 CC2 samples. Passed charge is a 64-bit value with a 32-bit time base, resettable by command. SRP and SRN tolerate larger positive voltages during overcurrent or short circuit, though the reading is then not accurate. Current is also sampled alongside each cell voltage for impedance work.

Die temperature comes from a delta-VBE measurement. Up to nine external thermistors can be used on TS1-TS3, CFETOFF, DFETOFF, ALERT, HDQ, DCHG and DDSG, each biased from REG18 through an internal 18 kΩ (for 10 kΩ parts such as Semitec 103-AT) or 180 kΩ pullup (for 200 kΩ parts such as Semitec 204AP-2), or none. The ADC uses REG18 as reference for these readings, so the result is ratiometric. Pullup values are measured at the factory; temperature is computed from a user-programmable polynomial. Each temperature has its own calibration offset.

Cell ADC offset and the TS, ADCIN, PACK, LD and VC16 gains are factory-trimmed. Each cell gain, the stack, PACK, LD and ADCIN gains, and offsets for cell and divider readings can be calibrated on the line; a written value replaces the trim. COV and CUV thresholds can be calibrated in CONFIG_UPDATE by applying the wanted level across VC16-VC15 and sending CAL_COV() or CAL_CUV(), which stores an override. Current offset and gain (CC Gain, Capacity Gain) are calibrated likewise.

Primary protections: cell UV and OV (and OV latch), OCC, three OCD tiers (and OCD latch), SCD (and SCD latch), under- and over-temperature in charge and discharge, internal and FET over-temperature, precharge timeout and host watchdog. CUV, COV, OCC, OCD1, OCD2 and SCD are comparator based; the rest run in firmware. Each can be enabled separately, along with whether it acts on the FETs. Recovery can be autonomous, held by the host, or the device can only alert.

Secondary checks (safety UV/OV, safety OCC/OCD, safety over-temperature of cells and FETs, copper deposition, SCD latch, voltage imbalance active and at rest, second-level protector, CHG and DSG FET failure, OTP, data and instruction ROM, LFO, reference, VSS, stuck mux, commanded PF and top-of-stack versus cell sum) raise a Permanent Fail. On PF the device can just flag it, hold the FETs off, or drive FUSE; it can write PF status to OTP, turn REG1/REG2 off or leave them, and go to DEEPSLEEP after fuse and OTP actions finish. PF conditions are checked once per second in NORMAL and SLEEP, after an alert and a programmable delay.

A charge pump with its capacitor from BAT to CP1 supplies the high-side CHG and DSG NFET drives at 5.5 V or 11 V overdrive. The lower setting dissipates less and suits FETs not rated for 15 V gate-source or with gate leakage; 11 V gives lower RDS(on). The pump takes about 60 ms to reach about 11 V with 470 nF, so it is best left running. In SLEEP the DSG FET may be driven in source-follower mode from BAT to save power, not for significant current. Series and parallel FET arrangements are supported. A larger CP1 limits the dip when large gates switch on: about 400 nF of gate with 2200 nF on CP1 drops 11 V to about 9 V.

Fully autonomous: faults turn FETs off and recovery turns them on with no host. Partly autonomous: the device turns FETs off and the host, through commands or the CFETOFF/DFETOFF pins, decides when they come back. Manual: the device raises ALERT and the host turns the FETs off by pin or command. A deasserted pin lets a FET back on only if nothing else is blocking it.

In series FET mode, if one FET is off, the other is on and current above a programmable threshold flows in the direction the off FET's body diode would conduct, the off FET is turned on for as long as that current lasts. Parallel mode disables this.

Below a programmable minimum cell voltage, charging goes through a high-side PFET on PCHG with a series resistor. With predischarge enabled, each DSG turn-on is preceded by a PDSG PFET with series resistor to charge the load slowly, then DSG turns on and PDSG off. PCHG and PDSG sink little current, so a 1 MΩ or larger gate-source resistor is called for.

After an SCD or OCD latch fault with DSG off, recovery can wait for load removal: a current source out of LD is pulsed on and off, and the fault clears if LD rises above 4 V. A remaining load heavier than about 20 kΩ keeps LD below that. LD usually connects to PACK+ through 10 kΩ, which counts in that load.

VREF1 serves the voltage ADC; VREF2 serves REG18, the oscillators and the coulomb counter, and can be checked by measuring REG18 against VREF1. REG18 powers only the internal circuits and needs its capacitor close to the pin. REG1 and REG2, each programmable to 1.8, 2.5, 3.0, 3.3 or 5.0 V and up to 45 mA, run from REGIN at about 5.5 V, supplied from outside or by the REG0 pre-regulator driving an external NPN from BREG. REGIN has a diode to BAT and must not exceed BAT. The LDOs and REG0 are off by default on BQ76952; off, REG1/REG2 are pulled to VSS by about 2.5 kΩ, or about 10 MΩ in SHUTDOWN. REG1 can be back-driven on the line to talk to the device and then programmed in OTP to start by itself.

ALERT, CFETOFF, DFETOFF, HDQ, DCHG and DDSG can be active-high outputs driven from REG1 or REG18, with optional weak pulldown or pullup to REG1. REG18 drive suits only very light loads (over 1 MΩ). ALERT can be the host interrupt (active low/hi-Z, active high or low, or inverted), HDQ (open drain), thermistor, ADCIN or GPO, with a mask choosing which flags raise it. DCHG and DDSG flag faults that would turn off CHG or DSG, for external or low-side FET circuits or as host interrupts.
Held low in normal operation. Driven high it resets most logic, including the serial interface, while keeping FET and FUSE states; held high for 1 s it starts SHUTDOWN.
Asserting CFETOFF turns off CHG and PCHG; DFETOFF turns off DSG and PDSG. DFETOFF can instead act as BOTHOFF, turning off all four, freeing CFETOFF for a thermistor.

FUSE can drive an NFET gate that blows a chemical fuse on PF, shared with a secondary protector; while not driving it is high impedance and can raise a PF when it sees the protector's high level. The fuse is blown only if the stack voltage (fuse between stack and FETs) or PACK voltage (fuse between FETs and PACK+) is above a programmed level, apart from special cases.

A current source from each VC pin to VSS is switched on for one ADC measurement time (3 ms default) at a programmable interval, giving an average of about 0.65 nA to 165 nA from the 55 µA typical. A floating input then drifts down and trips a fault and, later, a PF on that cell and the one above. It can cause some imbalance.

The LFO runs at about 262.144 kHz in NORMAL and about 32.768 kHz in SLEEP and DEEPSLEEP, where it may be turned off; it is factory trimmed. The 16.78 MHz HFO is locked to the LFO and starts as needed; it draws about 30 µA while on.

Full measurement and protection: current every 3 ms, cell voltages every 63 ms or slower, with a fast option that doubles voltage and CC2 rates at lower resolution. When CC1 current falls below a threshold the device can move to SLEEP.

Entered when current stays below a threshold and SLEEP is allowed. DSG stays on (charge pump or source follower), CHG optionally off. Comparator protections run as in NORMAL; ADC readings and temperature protections run at a programmable interval. The coulomb counter checks current every 12 ms. It leaves SLEEP on a fault, current, a charger (PACK above top of stack by a delta with the stack under a threshold), a subcommand, or RST_SHUT asserted under 1 s; fresh data may take about 1 s. A hysteresis time blocks re-entry.

Entered by subcommand (sent twice). FETs off, protections and measurements off; REG1 and REG2 may stay on, and the LFO may be kept running for faster response. Exits on subcommand, RST_SHUT under 1 s, or a charger raising LD past VWAKEONLD; it first runs a full measurement loop (about 250 ms plus the loop). BAT below VPORA - VPORA_HYS sends it to SHUTDOWN.

Lowest power: logic, LDOs and FETs off, registers lost. Entered by subcommand, RST_SHUT held high 1 s, low stack or minimum cell voltage, or high die temperature; FETs turn off after a delay and entry waits while LD stays above VWAKEONLD. TS2 is held at about 5 V through high impedance; pulling TS2 low or raising LD above VWAKEONLD wakes the device, which takes about 200-300 ms to enable FETs. A thermistor on TS2 can keep the device from ever fully shutting down. An auto re-shutdown timer guards against accidental wake in storage. Repeated memory errors after a watchdog reset end in SHUTDOWN. A hardware detector near 120°C die temperature can start shutdown.

Responder at 100 kHz or 400 kHz with optional CRC (polynomial x^8 + x^2 + x + 1, initial 0); default address 0x10 write / 0x11 read. Block writes and reads auto-increment the register address. Optional timeouts reset the interface if SCL stays low 25-35 ms (100 kHz) or 5-20 ms (400 kHz), or after cumulative clock stretching; SCL low for over 2 s always resets it. A bad CRC is NACKed. SWAP_TO_I2C() switches immediately.

BQ7695201 starts in SPI with CRC. Responder only, CPOL = 0, CPHA = 0. Transactions are 16 bits without CRC and 24 bits with CRC: R/W bit (write = 1) and 7-bit address, a data byte, then the CRC over both. Each transaction clocks out the result of the previous one. 0xFFFFFF means the oscillator was not running (it starts on SPI_CS falling and takes up to 50 µs), 0xFFFFAA a CRC error on the previous transaction, 0xFFFF00 a transaction not yet processed; these should be retried. Comm Idle Time keeps the HFO on 1-255 s after a transaction. Leave 50 µs or more between transactions; a subcommand needs about 200 µs to fill its 32-byte buffer. SPI_MISO may default to REG18 (1.8 V) drive; Settings:Configuration:SPI Configuration[MISO_REG1] switches it to REG1. Input filtering (about 200 ns) is on by default. SPI_CS low with SPI_SCLK static for 2 s resets the interface.

Single-wire, open-drain, return-to-one, on ALERT or HDQ. The host sends a break and break recovery, then an 8-bit command (7-bit code, R/W in bit 7), then 8 data bits from host or device, LSB first. No auto-increment, so each byte is its own transaction.

Passive balancing through internal switches or external FETs. Autonomous balancing uses a voltage-based algorithm on non-adjacent cells only and a limit on how many cells balance at once; the host may balance adjacent cells too, with a timer that stops balancing if the host goes quiet. Balancing pauses while the balanced cell and its neighbours, or the stack, are measured, so options slow the loop to raise average balancing current. A die temperature limit stops balancing; total device dissipation should still be worked out from ambient and package and held down by cell count and series resistance.

Cells may be connected in any time order in production, but each cell still goes to its own pair of VC pins in ascending order. VC0 must already be tied to VSS through its series resistor on the board, since it does not tolerate high voltage. Each VC pin has a diode to the next lower one; brief currents flow as cells attach, so the cell input capacitance should stay within the recommended values.
BAT normally takes the top of stack through a series diode and an RC filter; the BAT capacitor keeps the device alive while a short pulls the stack down until the FETs open.

The pre-regulator NPN collector can go to the stack or the midpoint of the FETs, with a diode in its collector to stop reverse flow from BREG during a pack short. The NPN is rated for a collector-emitter voltage up to the full charge voltage (68 V in the example) and must carry REG1's 45 mA (current limit up to about 80 mA); 10 MΩ from BREG to VSS stops leakage in SHUTDOWN. A series diode and capacitor on BAT keep the device running during a short; this diode and the BJT diode should not be shared. VC0-VC4 may go to -0.2 V, for example to read a second shunt. Without high-side FETs, PACK goes to the stack top through 10 kΩ and LD to VSS, or LD can be driven to wake the device. SRP and SRN take 100 Ω each with 100 nF (and optional 100 pF) across, routed short and symmetric on the same board side; 0.1 µF from each to VSS is optional. Protection FET voltage rating: roughly 5 V DC and 10 V peak for each cell in series.

Kelvin connections at the sense resistor matter most; use a resistor of 50 ppm/°C or better (1 mΩ in the example); parallel resistors are fine with good Kelvin sensing. Place the SRP/SRN filter parts next to the device, not the resistor, run the sense traces in parallel, and consider a ground plane around the filter. Put the REG18 capacitor right at the pin with low inductance to a VSS-connected plane. A zener and series resistor on each I2C line add ESD margin. The example board is 2.75 in × 3.9 in, two layers, cells wired in at the left edge and the pack at the top edge, with board-etched spark gaps (designators E).

CHG turns off by switching its gate to BAT. DSG discharges toward VSS but stops whenever DSG falls below LD (tied to PACK+ through a resistor), repeating in pulses for about 100-200 µs until it is within about 500 mV of LD; the gate-source resistor then finishes turning the FET off. The series gate resistor sets the speed: 100 Ω is fast but gives a large inductive spike at the stack top, 1 kΩ or 4.7 kΩ slower. With a CSD19536KCS (Ciss 9250 pF typical) and 1 kΩ the pulsing lasts about 170 µs.
